subject: math
title: Equal Groups and Sharing
seo_title: Grade 2 Equal Groups and Sharing Worksheets: Repeated Addition, Arrays, Halves (Free, Ontario)
standard_text: Represent multiplication as repeated equal groups, including groups of one half and one fourth, and solve related problems, using various tools and drawings
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on equal groups and sharing for the Ontario curriculum: repeated addition, arrays, groups of halves and fourths, sharing up to 12 equally and word problems. 100 questions with pictures and an answer key.
key_big: Equal groups are added again and again. Equal shares are all the same size.
key_sub: 3 groups of 4 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. 4 halves make 2 wholes. 12 shared equally on 3 plates is 4 on each plate.
body_html:
Equal groups

Look for equal groups. Count the groups. Count how many are in one group. Then add the same number again and again. This is repeated addition.

Example

There are 5 bags. Each bag has 2 apples. How many apples?

5 groups of 2. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.

Answer: 10 apples

Arrays

An array is objects in rows and columns. Rows go across. Columns go up and down. Add the rows or add the columns. You get the same total.

Groups of halves and fourths

You can make groups of parts, too. 2 halves make 1 whole. 4 fourths make 1 whole. Put the parts together to find how many wholes.

Example

3 children each eat half an orange. How many oranges do they eat?

3 halves. 2 halves make 1 whole, and 1 half is left over.

Answer: 1 and a half oranges

Sharing equally

To share equally, give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Every share must be the same.

Example

Share 8 crackers equally between 2 friends.

Give 1 to each friend, again and again. Each friend gets 4. Check: 4 + 4 = 8.

Answer: 4 crackers each

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the groups, not the objects: 3 groups of 4 = 3Count everything inside the rings: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12
Adding the two numbers: 3 groups of 4 = 7Add 4 once for each group: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12
Unequal sharing: 12 shared as 5, 4 and 3Every share must be the same: 4, 4 and 4
Counting halves as wholes: 6 halves = 6 orangesPut 2 halves together for each whole: 3 oranges

faq.q: What multiplication do Grade 2 students learn in Ontario?
faq.a: Grade 2 students show multiplication as repeated equal groups, such as 3 groups of 4 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12, using objects, arrays and drawings. They also make groups of one half and one fourth, like 4 halves make 2 wholes.

faq.q: Do Grade 2 students learn division in Ontario?
faq.a: Yes. Grade 2 students show division as sharing up to 12 items equally, using objects and drawings. The × and ÷ signs and the multiplication facts come in Grade 3.

faq.q: How do arrays help Grade 2 students with equal groups?
faq.a: An array puts equal groups in neat rows, so students can count by 2s, 5s or 10s instead of counting one by one. Adding the rows or the columns gives the same total.

faq.q: How can I help my child understand sharing equally?
faq.a: Use real things like crackers or blocks. Have your child give out one at a time to each plate until none are left, then check that every plate has the same number.

items.q: How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the rings: there are 3 groups. 2 is how many counters are in each group.
Count the rings: there are 4 groups. 5 is how many stars are in each group.

items.q: How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the rings: there are 5 groups. 3 is how many blocks are in each group.

items.q: How many counters are in each group?
items.e: Look inside one ring. It has 5 counters. Every group is the same.
Look inside one ring. It has 2 stars. Every group is the same.

items.q: How many blocks are in each group?
items.e: Look inside one ring. It has 3 blocks. Every group is the same.

items.q: How many counters are there in all?
items.e: 2 groups of 3: 3 + 3 = 6. (Not 2: that is just the number of groups. Not 2 + 3 = 5: that adds the groups to one group.)
5 groups of 2: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10. (Not 5: that is just the number of groups. Not 5 + 2 = 7: that adds the groups to one group.)

items.q: How many blocks are there in all?
items.e: 3 groups of 5: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15. (Not 3: that is just the number of groups. Not 3 + 5 = 8: that adds the groups to one group.)

items.q: How many counters are there in all?
items.e: 2 groups of 10: 10 + 10 = 20. (Not 2: that is just the number of groups. Not 2 + 10 = 12: that adds the groups to one group.)
3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. (Not 3: that is just the number of groups. Not 3 + 4 = 7: that adds the groups to one group.)

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 3 groups. Each group has 5. Add 5, 3 times: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 4 groups. Each group has 2. Add 2, 4 times: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8.
There are 3 groups. Each group has 10. Add 10, 3 times: 10 + 10 + 10 = 30.

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 4 groups. Each group has 3. Add 3, 4 times: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12.

items.q: Which picture shows 3 groups of 4?
items.e: A has 3 rings with 4 counters in each. Check both numbers: count the groups, then count inside one group. All the groups must be equal.
D has 2 rings with 5 stars in each. Check both numbers: count the groups, then count inside one group. All the groups must be equal.

items.q: Which picture shows 5 groups of 2?
items.e: A has 5 rings with 2 blocks in each. Check both numbers: count the groups, then count inside one group. All the groups must be equal.

items.q: Which is the same as 3 groups of 5?
items.e: 3 groups of 5 means 5, three times: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Count by 5s. How many are in 4 groups of 5?
items.e: Say one 5 for each group: 5, 10, 15, 20. 4 groups of 5 is 20. (9 comes from 4 + 5.)

items.q: How many rows are in this array?
items.e: Rows go across. Count from top to bottom: 3 rows. Each row has 5.

items.q: How many rows are in this array?
items.e: Rows go across. Count from top to bottom: 4 rows. Each row has 3.
Columns go up and down. Count from left to right: 4 columns. Each column has 2.

items.q: How many columns are in this array?
items.e: Columns go up and down. Count from left to right: 2 columns. Each column has 5.

items.q: How many blocks are in the array?
items.e: 2 rows of 5: 5 + 5 = 10. (Not 2 + 5 = 7: that adds the rows to one row.)

items.q: How many counters are in the array?
items.e: 4 rows of 2: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. (Not 4 + 2 = 6: that adds the rows to one row.)
3 rows of 10: 10 + 10 + 10 = 30. (Not 3 + 10 = 13: that adds the rows to one row.)

items.q: How many blocks are in the array?
items.e: 5 rows of 5: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 25. (Not 5 + 5 = 10: that adds the rows to one row.)

items.q: How many counters are in the array?
items.e: 3 rows of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. (Not 3 + 4 = 7: that adds the rows to one row.)

items.q: Add the rows. Which addition matches?
items.e: Each row has 3. There are 2 rows. So add 3, 2 times: 3 + 3 = 6.
Each row has 5. There are 4 rows. So add 5, 4 times: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20.

items.q: Add the rows. Which addition matches?
items.e: Each row has 10. There are 3 rows. So add 10, 3 times: 10 + 10 + 10 = 30.

items.q: Add the columns. Which addition matches?
items.e: Each column has 5. There are 3 columns. So add 5, 3 times: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15. Adding the rows gives 15 too.
Each column has 3. There are 4 columns. So add 3, 4 times: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12. Adding the rows gives 12 too.

items.q: Add the columns. Which addition matches?
items.e: Each column has 2. There are 5 columns. So add 2, 5 times: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10. Adding the rows gives 10 too.

items.q: The array is split into two parts. How many counters are there in all?
items.e: Top part: 5 + 5 = 10. Bottom part: 5 + 5 = 10. Add the parts: 10 + 10 = 20.

items.q: The array is split into two parts. How many counters are there in all?
items.e: Top part: 3 + 3 = 6. Bottom part: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. Add the parts: 6 + 9 = 15.

items.q: Owen says 2 rows of 5 and 5 rows of 2 have different totals. Is he right?
items.e: 5 + 5 = 10 and 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10. No. Both are 10. It is the same array, turned.

items.q: Which array has the same number of dots as 3 rows of 4?
items.e: 3 rows of 4 is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. 4 rows of 3 is 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12. Turning an array keeps the total.

items.q: An array has 5 rows of 10. Count by 10s. How many dots?
items.e: Say one 10 for each row: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. That is 50 dots. (15 comes from 5 + 10.)

items.q: Here are 4 orange halves. How many whole oranges do they make?
items.e: 2 halves make 1 whole. Put the halves in pairs: 4 halves make 2 wholes. (4 counts the pieces, not the whole oranges.)

items.q: Here are 6 orange halves. How many whole oranges do they make?
items.e: 2 halves make 1 whole. Put the halves in pairs: 6 halves make 3 wholes. (6 counts the pieces, not the whole oranges.)

items.q: Here are 8 orange halves. How many whole oranges do they make?
items.e: 2 halves make 1 whole. Put the halves in pairs: 8 halves make 4 wholes. (8 counts the pieces, not the whole oranges.)

items.q: Here are 10 orange halves. How many whole oranges do they make?
items.e: 2 halves make 1 whole. Put the halves in pairs: 10 halves make 5 wholes. (10 counts the pieces, not the whole oranges.)

items.q: Here are 3 orange halves. How many whole oranges do they make?
items.e: Make pairs: 1 pair of halves makes 1 whole. One half is left over. That is 1 and a half.

items.q: Here are 5 orange halves. How many whole oranges do they make?
items.e: Make pairs: 2 pairs of halves make 2 wholes. One half is left over. That is 2 and a half.

items.q: Here are 7 orange halves. How many whole oranges do they make?
items.e: Make pairs: 3 pairs of halves make 3 wholes. One half is left over. That is 3 and a half.

items.q: Each piece is one fourth of a pizza. How many whole pizzas do these 4 pieces make?
items.e: 4 fourths make 1 whole pizza. Make groups of 4: 4 fourths make 1 whole. (Not 2: it takes 4 fourths, not 2, to make a whole.)

items.q: Each piece is one fourth of a pizza. How many whole pizzas do these 8 pieces make?
items.e: 4 fourths make 1 whole pizza. Make groups of 4: 8 fourths make 2 wholes. (Not 4: it takes 4 fourths, not 2, to make a whole.)

items.q: Each piece is one fourth of a pizza. How many whole pizzas do these 12 pieces make?
items.e: 4 fourths make 1 whole pizza. Make groups of 4: 12 fourths make 3 wholes. (Not 6: it takes 4 fourths, not 2, to make a whole.)

items.q: Each piece is one fourth of a pizza. How much pizza is this?
items.e: 4 fourths make 1 whole. 5 fourths is 4 fourths and 1 more: 1 and 1 fourth. (2 and a half would be right for halves, not fourths.)

items.q: Each piece is one fourth of a pizza. How much pizza is this?
items.e: 4 fourths make 1 whole. 7 fourths is 4 fourths and 3 more: 1 and 3 fourths. (3 and a half would be right for halves, not fourths.)

items.q: These 2 oranges are cut in half. How many halves are there?
items.e: Each orange is cut into 2 halves. Count by 2s: 2, 4. That is 4 halves.

items.q: These 4 oranges are cut in half. How many halves are there?
items.e: Each orange is cut into 2 halves. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. That is 8 halves.

items.q: These 2 pizzas are cut into fourths. How many fourths are there?
items.e: Each pizza is cut into 4 fourths. 4 + 4 = 8 fourths.

items.q: These 3 pizzas are cut into fourths. How many fourths are there?
items.e: Each pizza is cut into 4 fourths. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 fourths.

items.q: There is half a sandwich on each plate. How many whole sandwiches is that?
items.e: 3 groups of one half. 2 halves make 1 whole, and 1 half is left: 1 and a half sandwiches.

items.q: There is half a sandwich on each plate. How many whole sandwiches is that?
items.e: 6 groups of one half. Every 2 halves make 1 whole: 6 halves make 3 wholes.

items.q: What do 4 groups of one half make?
items.e: One half + one half = 1 whole. Do it twice: 4 halves make 2 wholes.

items.q: How many fourths make 2 wholes?
items.e: 4 fourths make 1 whole. 2 wholes need 4 + 4 = 8 fourths. (4 fourths make only 1 whole.)

items.q: Share these 6 counters equally between 2 plates. How many does each plate get?
items.e: Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each plate gets 3. Check: 3 + 3 = 6.
Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each plate gets 4. Check: 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: Share these 9 blocks equally between 3 plates. How many does each plate get?
items.e: Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each plate gets 3. Check: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

items.q: Share these 12 counters equally between 3 plates. How many does each plate get?
items.e: Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each plate gets 4. Check: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each bag gets 2. Check: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10.

items.q: Share these 12 blocks equally between 4 bags. How many does each bag get?
items.e: Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each bag gets 3. Check: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12.

items.q: Share these 8 counters equally between 4 bags. How many does each bag get?
items.e: Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each bag gets 2. Check: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8.
Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each bag gets 6. Check: 6 + 6 = 12.

items.q: Share 12 counters equally between 4 plates. Which picture shows this?
items.e: Sharing between 4 plates means 4 plates, all the same. D has 4 plates of 3. 3 plates of 4 is the wrong number of plates. 4, 3, 3 and 2 is not equal. 4 plates of 2 shares only 8.
Sharing between 2 plates means 2 plates with the same amount. A has 5 and 5. 6 and 4 is not fair. 5 plates of 2 is the wrong number of plates. 4 and 4 shares only 8.

items.q: Share 6 blocks equally between 3 plates. Which picture shows this?
items.e: Sharing between 3 plates means 3 plates with the same amount. A has 2, 2 and 2. 2 plates of 3 is the wrong number of plates. 3, 2 and 1 is not equal. 1, 1 and 1 shares only 3.

items.q: Ava wants 10 counters shared equally on 2 plates. How many counters must move?
items.e: 10 shared between 2 is 5 each. Move 1 from the 6 to the 4: 5 and 5. (Moving 2 would just swap the two amounts.)

items.q: Leah wants 10 counters shared equally on 2 plates. How many counters must move?
items.e: 10 shared between 2 is 5 each. Move 2 from the 7 to the 3: 5 and 5. (Moving 4 would just swap the two amounts.)

items.q: Jayden wants 6 counters shared equally on 2 plates. How many counters must move?
items.e: 6 shared between 2 is 3 each. Move 2 from the 5 to the 1: 3 and 3. (Moving 4 would just swap the two amounts.)

items.q: Mei shared 12 counters on 3 plates. What went wrong?
items.e: 5 + 4 + 3 = 12, but equal shares must be the same. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12, so each plate should get 4.

items.q: Benjamin had to share 12 counters equally on 3 plates. What went wrong?
items.e: The shares are equal, but there should be 3 plates, not 2. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12, so use 3 plates of 4.

items.q: Which shows 12 shared equally between 3?
items.e: Between 3 means 3 shares, all the same size. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12, so 4, 4 and 4. 5, 4 and 3 also makes 12, but it is not equal.

items.q: Which shows 10 shared equally between 2?
items.e: Equal shares are the same size. 5 + 5 = 10, so 5 and 5. 6 and 4 also make 10, but they are not equal.

items.q: Counters are shared on 4 plates. Each plate gets 3. How many counters were shared?
items.e: 4 plates of 3: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12. (7 comes from 4 + 3.)

items.q: Stars are shared between 3 bags. Each bag gets 2. How many stars were shared?
items.e: 3 bags of 2: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. (5 comes from 3 + 2.)

sets.title: Equal groups and sharing word problems

items.q: A pair of mitts is 2 mitts. Kai has 4 pairs. How many mitts is that?
items.e: 4 groups of 2: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 mitts. (6 comes from 4 + 2.)

items.q: A canoe holds 2 people. 5 canoes go out on the lake. How many people is that?
items.e: 5 groups of 2. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. That is 10 people.

items.q: A Canada goose has 2 legs. There are 7 geese on the pond. How many legs is that?
items.e: 7 groups of 2. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. That is 14 legs.

items.q: A moose has 4 legs. There are 3 moose in the field. How many legs is that?
items.e: 3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 legs. (7 comes from 3 + 4.)
4 groups of 5. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 muffins.

items.q: A dime is 10¢. Hana has 6 dimes. How much money is that?
A nickel is 5¢. Sofia has 5 nickels. How much money is that?
items.e: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. 5 nickels is 25¢.

items.q: Chairs for the class show are set out in 3 rows of 5. How many chairs is that?
items.e: 3 rows of 5: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15 chairs.

items.q: In gym class, 12 students make 2 equal soccer teams. How many students are on each team?
items.e: 12 shared between 2 teams: 6 + 6 = 12. Each team has 6 students.

items.q: Aiden shares 8 stickers equally with a friend. How many stickers does each of them get?
items.e: There are 2 people. 8 shared between 2: 4 + 4 = 8. Each gets 4 stickers.

items.q: Share 12 maple cookies equally among 4 friends. How many cookies does each friend get?
items.e: Give out one at a time until none are left. 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12. Each friend gets 3 cookies.

items.q: A teacher shares 10 markers equally between 5 tables. How many markers go on each table?
items.e: 10 shared between 5: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10. Each table gets 2 markers.

items.q: Ethan has 6 crackers. He shares them equally with 2 friends. How many crackers does each person get?
items.e: Ethan and 2 friends are 3 people. 6 shared between 3: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. Each gets 2 crackers. (3 each would be for only 2 people.)

items.q: At lunch, 5 children each eat half a sandwich. How many whole sandwiches do they eat?
items.e: 5 halves. 2 halves make 1 whole, so 4 halves make 2 wholes. 1 half is left: 2 and a half sandwiches.

items.q: A pizza is cut into fourths. 8 children each get one fourth. How many pizzas is that?
items.e: 4 fourths make 1 pizza. 8 fourths make 4 + 4, so 2 pizzas. (4 pizzas would mean 2 fourths make a whole.)

items.q: Zoe eats half an apple each day for 6 days. How many whole apples is that?
items.e: 6 halves. Every 2 halves make 1 whole: 6 halves make 3 apples.

items.q: A pancake recipe uses half a cup of milk. Ava makes it 4 times. How many cups of milk does she use?
items.e: 4 groups of one half. 2 halves make 1 cup, so 4 halves make 2 cups.

items.q: Nathan has 2 bags of 5 marbles. He gives away 3 marbles. How many marbles are left?
items.e: Step 1: 5 + 5 = 10 marbles. Step 2: 10 − 3 = 7 marbles. (4 comes from 2 + 5 − 3.)

items.q: Chloe says, “3 bags of 4 apples is 7 apples.” What went wrong?
items.e: 3 + 4 = 7 adds the bags to one bag. 3 bags of 4 is 4 + 4 + 4. She added 3 + 4. It is 12.

items.q: Noah has 3 bags with 4 granola bars in each. He shares all the bars equally with a friend. How many bars does each of them get?
items.e: Step 1: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 bars. Step 2: 12 shared between 2 people is 6 + 6. Each gets 6 bars.
